page: Microsoft Azure E48d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 CPU package incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and VAES instructions. The server includes 384 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 1933 GB of local SSD temporary storage. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs provisioned on this instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong processing efficiency across memory-intensive and parallel enterprise workloads. The E48d_v5 achieved a PassMark CPU score of 50,821.1 and a PassMark memory score of 2,851.15, placing both in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Cryptographic testing also performed well, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 43,841.1, assisted by hardware-level vector instructions. In throughput evaluations, uncached memory bandwidth sustained 150.89 GB/sec for reads and 64.31 GB/sec for writes, while Redis key-value workloads reached 44.0 million SET operations per second.

Database operations registered a strong PassMark score of 23,256.75, making the system effective for transaction-heavy database engines. Compute benchmarks like stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core placed within the middle percentiles, illustrating balanced rather than class-leading pure raw compute. While small-parameter language model generation ran efficiently at 279.48 tokens per second, large 70B parameter models scored in the lowest quartile at 2.69 tokens per second, highlighting that unaccelerated CPU execution is inefficient for large-scale generative deep learning tasks.

The inclusion of 1933 GB of local solid-state storage gives the instance strong qualitative value for caching tiers, scratch space, and high-speed temporary file operations without incurring network storage penalties. With its large memory footprint and dedicated cores, Microsoft Azure E48d_v5 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise resource planning applications, and heavy multi-threaded ETL pipelines.

It provides 384 GB of memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and integrates 1933 GB of local SSD temporary storage without attached GPUs. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. Performance evaluations indicate strong results in PassMark memory testing, CPU encryption, and database operational benchmarks, alongside sustained memory bandwidth of 150.89 GB/sec read and 64.31 GB/sec write. Standard multi-core compute tests place within average tiers, while large language model inference shows low execution speeds due to CPU constraints.
